_metadata.description: NCAA March Madness Tournament Bracket Data - Seeds Only

format_notes.bracket_structure: Standard 64-team bracket (68 teams from 2011, but First Four play-in games resolve to 64 before main bracket)
format_notes.r64_matchup_order: The 8 first-round matchups in each region follow standard bracket order: 1v16, 8v9, 5v12, 4v13, 6v11, 3v14, 7v10, 2v15
format_notes.r64_winners: Seeds of the 8 winners from the Round of 64, in matchup order (positions 1-8 correspond to the 8 matchups above)
format_notes.r32_winners: Seeds of the 4 winners from the Round of 32. Matchups are: winner of 1v16 game vs winner of 8v9 game, winner of 5v12 vs 4v13, winner of 6v11 vs 3v14, winner of 7v10 vs 2v15
format_notes.s16_winners: Seeds of the 2 Sweet 16 winners (top half vs bottom half of region bracket)
format_notes.e8_winner: Seed of the Elite Eight winner (region champion)
format_notes.f4: Final Four - two semifinal games, each showing the two teams (seed + region) and the winner
format_notes.championship: National Championship game showing both finalists (seed + region) and the winner
format_notes.region_names: Region names varied over the years. Some years used city names (2004-2006), most used East/South/Midwest/West or similar

_metadata.how_to_rebuild_bracket: For each region, start with seeds 1-16 in standard bracket order (1v16, 8v9, 5v12, 4v13, 6v11, 3v14, 7v10, 2v15). The r64_winners tell you which seed won each of those 8 games. The r32_winners tell you the 4 second-round winners. The s16_winners are the 2 Sweet 16 winners. The e8_winner is the region champion. Then f4 and championship show the Final Four and title game with region tags to distinguish same-seeded teams.
